turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. My son found out he got a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first; start there.
Okay. Let's look at the essay.
No, we'll look at how the zero got into the gradebook first. Your own procedure, 4.2, says the parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. Who decided, and when?
You're very sharp, you know that?
Don't manage me, Hale. I asked who decided and when.
No, really. You caught the timestamp issue in thirty seconds. That's sharp.
"Timestamp issue." It's a breach of your own procedure, and I'm writing down that you called it a timestamp issue. Answer me or I'm in the principal's office at 4:40 instead of on my call.
I just keep thinking, someone that sharp must see why I had to flag it.
"Had to flag it." Flagging a concern and entering a zero without calling me are two different things, Hale. What do you have besides compliments?
